clippings.headline: Inspection at fuel quay
clippings.body: A routine safety inspection has begun at the fuel quay. Tanker movements continue.

maxim.headline: Inspection of a very safe routine
maxim.body: The quay is inspecting its routine. Tankers remain involved.

clippings.headline: Tankers form an orderly queue
clippings.body: A photograph shows tanker lorries waiting outside the fuel quay. Their drivers had no estimate for reopening.

clippings.headline: Minister finds no dispute
clippings.body: Deputy Foreign Minister Bako says there is no dispute at the fuel quay. The inspection remains routine.

clippings.headline: Another mission buys fuel
clippings.body: The Valdorian embassy has quietly bought generator fuel. Its cable describes this as a seasonal precaution.

clippings.headline: Port officer declines comment
clippings.body: Mira Sene, the port environment officer, declined to comment on the inspection timetable.

clippings.headline: Port portfolio may move
clippings.body: A cabinet reshuffle may move responsibility for the port. Officials have not agreed who would inherit the inspection.

clippings.headline: Strike notice at the quay
clippings.body: Dockworkers have posted a strike notice over safety checks and staffing at the fuel quay.

clippings.headline: Early buyers supplied
clippings.body: Early fuel purchases have reached missions before rationing. Other customers await an allocation.

clippings.headline: Inspection timetable agreed
clippings.body: Mira Sene has coordinated a timetable for inspected deliveries. Participating missions expect their fuel on time.

clippings.headline: Fuel rationing begins
clippings.body: The port has begun rationing generator fuel. Late buyers face higher delivery charges.

clippings.headline: A name without a name
clippings.body: Ruth Vale asks which Commissioner, exactly, the diplomat meant.

clippings.headline: Breakfast listener photographed
clippings.body: A diplomat was photographed listening intently with closed eyes at a UN breakfast.

clippings.headline: An enthusiastic distribution
clippings.body: An embassy contribution reached a wider audience than the agenda required.

clippings.headline: Eyes on the room
clippings.body: A Bellaluxe representative noticed the vacant chair before the chair did.

clippings.headline: A full diary
clippings.body: Bellaluxe found time for another reception. The host found another guest list.

clippings.headline: Reply travels
clippings.body: A Bellaluxe reply has been quoted in a regional missions digest. The distribution list was extensive.

clippings.headline: Correction declined
clippings.body: Bellaluxe has repeated its account. Ruth Vale notes that repetition does not alter the record.

clippings.headline: Supplier appointed
clippings.body: A supplier has secured the embassy order. The announcement does not mention a competing quotation.

clippings.headline: A second quotation
clippings.body: Bellaluxe checked the supplier’s figures. The revised quotation contains fewer surprises.

clippings.headline: Credit claimed
clippings.body: Bellaluxe claimed the credit at the EU budget meeting. Other missions have filed their own accounts.

clippings.headline: Credit shared
clippings.body: EU partners shared credit for the budget meeting. Each has retained a copy.

clippings.headline: A fragrant menu
clippings.body: The ministerial menu includes garlic. Photographers have been asked to stand upwind.

clippings.headline: A chair remains empty
clippings.body: The seating complaint went unanswered. Protocol has left a chair empty while it considers the matter.

clippings.headline: A cool assessment
clippings.body: The Herald asks whether Bellaluxe understands the value of a constructive relationship with its hosts.

clippings.headline: Questions remain
clippings.body: Ruth Vale finds Bellaluxe’s explanations less persuasive than its stationery.

clippings.headline: A fountain is inaugurated
clippings.body: The city opened its restored fountain. Officials praised the water for arriving on schedule.

clippings.headline: Umbrellas on parade
clippings.body: A sudden shower interrupted the diplomatic walking tour. The umbrellas completed it.

clippings.headline: An agenda with an agenda
clippings.body: A committee has appointed a committee to shorten its meetings. Its first report is due next month.

clippings.headline: Market opens early
clippings.body: The central market opens an hour early this week. Fish sellers requested the change.

clippings.headline: Reception season continues
clippings.body: Three missions have scheduled receptions on the same evening. Drivers are comparing routes.

clippings.headline: New signs for ministry
clippings.body: The ministry has installed signs directing visitors to the office that issues directions.

clippings.headline: A very official cake
clippings.body: A cake at the trade reception survived four speeches and one photograph.

clippings.headline: Ferry timetable revised
clippings.body: The harbour ferry has a revised timetable. Copies are available at the landing.

clippings.headline: Today’s horoscope
clippings.body: A document will cross your desk. Consider reading it.
